narrative.overview:
Logomocja is a working studio printed like a Polish railway timetable, the yellow *Rozkład jazdy: Odjazdy* poster on every station wall. The yellow belongs to the shell: the top bar, the primary action, the current step. Everything structural is set in timetable black: hairline rules between rows, a heavier rule under every column head, small condensed uppercase labels, and bold condensed figures that read like departure hours. The program's run is the schedule. Every executed statement takes a row, the row in progress rides the yellow bar, and a failure is a red footnote.

The drawing is the reward, so the turtle's ink is quarantined on the plate: an almost-white sheet by day, a charcoal sheet by night, ruled as a real coordinate field. The shell never borrows the turtle's colours, and the plate never borrows the shell's furniture beyond its view controls and a tabular status strip.

Density is a working tool's density, not a poster's. Controls are the standard web controls a learner already knows (buttons, a segmented switch, a range slider, tabs, menus), in a print vocabulary: flat, squared, bordered, never glossy.
keyCharacteristics: Timetable yellow carries the shell; black ink and hairline rules carry structure.
Condensed uppercase labels and bold condensed tabular figures, Archivo throughout the UI.
Code in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono, chosen for learners' legibility.
The run shown as a departure board: one row per step, current row on the yellow bar.
Turtle colours appear only on the drawing plate, thumbnails and colour swatches.
Flat print: borders instead of shadows, 3–5px corners.

rules.name: The Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Turtle ink (`#16866a` and every colour a program sets) lives only on the plate, in thumbnails and in colour swatches next to the literal that sets it. The shell is yellow, black, grey and red.

rules.name: The Footnote Rule
rules.body: Red is reserved for errors. A red element that does not report a problem is a bug.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yellow is a ground, never a text or line colour on white. On yellow, use ink.

rules.name: The Departure Hour Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes while a program runs is tabular. Step numbers are bold and condensed, so the board never jitters.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: UI, headings and data share Archivo; only program text is monospace. Never use mono to make something look technical.

rules.name: The Border-Or-Shadow Rule
rules.body: An element declares its elevation once: a border (view controls, notices, chips, buttons) or a shadow (light popovers, toasts), never both.

dos: Do keep yellow on the shell and on state (current row, executing token, primary action, passed stamp).
Do put a 2px ink rule under every column head, pane title and page head, and hairlines between rows.
Do set changing numbers in tabular figures and step numbers in bold condensed Archivo.
Do face lists of programs and tasks with thumbnails of their real drawings.
Do report errors in red with the line, the column and a fix in Polish, at the exact token.
Do keep copy gender-neutral in Polish: present tense, imperatives or impersonal forms, no gendered past tense.
donts: Don't let turtle colours leak into the shell (no green buttons because the default pen is green).
Don't use red for anything that is not an error.
Don't set yellow text or yellow lines on white.
Don't round corners beyond 5px, or add shadows to panes, buttons or panels.
Don't use monospace outside program text, trace commands and identifiers.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow line above a heading; metadata follows the title.
